inputs.text: [happily] Listen, Wex: amphibians now live on land. [curious] But they're still missing something.
[calm] They always have to go back near water to lay their eggs, [softly] or else the eggs dry out. [serious] So life invents a solution.
[excited][amazed] An egg with a hard shell, [gasps] that keeps the water sealed inside! [happily] And there you have the very first true reptiles.
[amazed] So they can lay eggs anywhere they want?
[playful] Exactly! Even far from water, right in a desert. [calm] This time is called the Permian.
[curious] And are the continents like today?
[serious][calm] Not at all! All the continents are stuck together into one giant block: Pangea. [softly] That means "all the Earth," in Greek.
[amazed] Around it, one single huge ocean. [pauses] And at the center of the block, so far from the sea that the climate turns very, very dry: a giant desert.
[gasps] Were there dinosaurs, in that desert?

[chuckles][softly] Not yet! [playful] There is an animal with a big sail on its back, Dimetrodon, [serious] but it's not a dinosaur: it's a distant cousin of mammals. [calm] Dinosaurs will arrive forty million years later.
[nervous] What happens next, in that desert?
[serious][softly] The climate keeps getting drier, and harder. [pauses] And far beneath our feet, something is brewing...
